content:
The image shows a single leaf that is largely tan/brown and desiccated, with the petiole/stem end showing greenish tissue with irregular dark, sunken or necrotic lesions. The leaf has lost most of its green color, appearing withered and dead.

Key observations:
- Tan-brown, shriveled leaf — dead/dying tissue
- Dark, irregular necrotic spots on the stem/petiole area
- The lesions appear sunken and angular — consistent with anthracnose
- No white powdery coating (rules out Powdery_Mildew)
- No black sooty coating (rules out Sooty_Mould)
- Die_Back typically progresses from shoot tips inward; this looks more like discrete lesion spots rather than tip dieback
- The dark, irregular, sunken lesions on the petiole and leaf surface are classic anthracnose symptoms
